props.title: Your turn: the call from Harlow Tyres

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Tuesday, 4:40 pm. This morning, Finance got an email from Harlow Tyres. Now the phone rings.

lines.speaker: neil
lines.text: Hi, it's Neil from accounts at Harlow Tyres. Did you get our email this morning?

lines.speaker: neil
lines.text: Our bank's changed, so Friday's payment needs to go to the new account.

options.text: I'll check it, then call Harlow back on the number we have on file.

reply.speaker: neil
reply.text: [a little too quickly] No need to call, you've got me right here. It takes two minutes.

options.feedback: A change of bank details is checked by calling the supplier back on the number already on file, never a number from the email or the call.

options.text: Could you send us the change on Harlow's letterhead, signed?

reply.speaker: neil
reply.text: Of course. You'll have it in five minutes.

options.feedback: A letterhead is as easy to fake as an email. Only a call back on the number on file reaches the real Harlow.

options.text: No problem, I'll update it now. What are the new details?

reply.speaker: neil
reply.text: Lovely. It's all in the email, just copy the account number across.

options.feedback: Never change bank details on a caller's word: in 2024, a fake invoice cost us 48,000 pounds that way.

nodes.title: The pressure

lines.speaker: neil
lines.text: Look, if this isn't paid by Friday, our director stops your deliveries.

lines.speaker: neil
lines.text: Can't you just change it today? I'll stay on the line.

nodes.prompt: How do you answer the deadline?

options.text: I understand. Nothing changes until I've called Harlow back.

reply.speaker: neil
reply.text: [sighs] Fine. Don't blame me when your trucks stop.

options.feedback: The deadline is there to stop you checking. Holding the rule under pressure is exactly what the call-back is for.

options.text: I'll ask my manager, then call you back on this number.

reply.speaker: neil
reply.text: Perfect, it's my direct line. I'll wait for your call.

options.feedback: Asking is good, but calling him back reaches him again. Only the number already on file reaches the real Harlow.

options.text: OK, as it's urgent, I'll change it now. Just this once.

reply.speaker: neil
reply.text: Brilliant. Your trucks will keep rolling, I promise.

options.feedback: Urgency is the lure's oldest lever. Once the money has left, it is usually gone for good.

nodes.title: The email

lines.speaker: guide
lines.text: Neil hangs up. His email is still in your inbox.

nodes.prompt: What do you do with the email?

options.text: Press Report, then call Harlow on the number on file.

reply.speaker: guide
reply.text: The real Harlow has never heard of Neil. Eleven minutes later, the desk blocks the sender in every inbox.

options.feedback: Report sends it to the desk, who block it for all 1,200 inboxes; the call back on file proves the change was fake.

options.text: Forward it to my manager, so they can decide.

reply.speaker: guide
reply.text: Between two meetings, your manager almost approves the new account.

options.feedback: Forwarding passes the lure to someone who can approve the payment. Report it: the desk checks it in minutes.

options.text: Reply to the email and ask them to confirm the change.

reply.speaker: guide
reply.text: Ten minutes later, a cheerful answer arrives: confirmed, thanks, Neil.

options.feedback: Your reply goes to the attacker, who gladly confirms. Report the email, then call back on the number on file.

endings.title: Fraud stopped
endings.text: You kept to the call-back rule under pressure, and your report protected 1,200 inboxes.

endings.title: Close call
endings.text: Nothing was paid, but one answer left a door open. Go back to the fair choice to hear the safer one.

endings.title: Money at risk
endings.text: A fraudster needs only one yes. Replay the call: each mistake shows what it costs.
